The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
We treat the board as a multiset of 2100 entries.

For a move on \(a,b\), write \(a=gx,\ b=gy\) with \(\gcd(x,y)=1\), where \(g=\gcd(a,b)\). Then

\[
\gcd(a,b)+\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)=g+gxy,
\]
so
\[
(g+gxy)-(gx+gy)=g(x-1)(y-1)\ge 0.
\]

Thus the total sum of the numbers on the board strictly increases exactly when the move changes the board. Since the product of all numbers is invariant, the sum is bounded, so Mark eventually reaches a state where every pair of numbers is comparable by divisibility. Therefore the final multiset can be ordered as a divisibility chain

\[
F_1\mid F_2\mid \cdots \mid F_{2100}.
\]

For each prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-adic valuations is invariant, because replacing \(a,b\) by \(\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\) replaces \(v_p(a),v_p(b)\) by their minimum and maximum. In the final chain, the valuations \(v_p(F_i)\) are nondecreasing, so \(v_p(F_i)\) is the \(i\)-th smallest value among \(v_p(1),v_p(2),\dots,v_p(2100)\).

The 2026th smallest final entry is the \(75\)th largest entry, since \(2100-2026+1=75\). For a prime \(p\), its exponent in \(F_{2026}\) is the largest \(t\) such that at least \(75\) of the numbers \(1,2,\dots,2100\) are divisible by \(p^t\), i.e.

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^t}\right\rfloor \ge 75.
\]

Now compute:

- \(p=2\): \(\lfloor 2100/16\rfloor=131\ge75\), but \(\lfloor 2100/32\rfloor=65<75\), so exponent \(4\).
- \(p=3\): \(\lfloor 2100/27\rfloor=77\ge75\), but \(\lfloor 2100/81\rfloor=25<75\), so exponent \(3\).
- \(p=5\): \(\lfloor 2100/25\rfloor=84\ge75\), but \(\lfloor 2100/125\rfloor=16<75\), so exponent \(2\).
- For \(p=7,11,13,17,19,23\), \(\lfloor 2100/p\rfloor\ge75\) but \(\lfloor 2100/p^2\rfloor<75\), so exponent \(1\).
- For \(p\ge29\), \(\lfloor 2100/p\rfloor\le72<75\), so exponent \(0\).

Thus

\[
F_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

Its number of positive divisors is

\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
